findings.before: The first line places a limit upon ordinary claims to know the Creator’s making. The second does not answer with a more impressive human title. It names the Master and the servant in the Master’s presence. Knowledge here is relational: the servant remains a servant while receiving understanding. In the preceding verses, coolness and the fire that consumes the world have been central. That context helps the reader hear this brief statement as wonder before the Creator’s working, while its compressed wording still deserves careful grammatical review.
findings.after: The first line asks the reader to recognize something about the Creator’s making. In the contextual reading used here, its unstated subject is the consuming fire described in 175: that force, too, belongs to creation. The second line names the Master and the servant who remains in the Master’s presence. The servant’s knowing therefore grows from a relationship of devotion, not from becoming an independent master of creation. This connection with the preceding verse should remain attributed, since the short opening does not repeat the word for fire.
findings.reason: Explain the selected reading without making the omitted referent look explicit or merely discussing incomprehensible creation.

findings.before: Sun and moon enter the verse before its return to dust. Their light gives the body an image of possibility, while the second line names the encounter that matters: Guru and Gobind. The ending deliberately recalls Salok 178, so the two should be read together. Bodily appearance and brightness cannot secure permanence, but the short life is still a place for spiritual meeting. The precise force of the opening’s compressed syntax needs scholarly attention. The draft therefore keeps the light image without turning it into an account of anatomy or cosmic origins.
findings.after: The opening links the body’s formation with the rising of sun and moon, rather than simply describing daylight falling upon it. In the attributed reading used here, their warmth and coolness picture qualities fulfilled through meeting Guru and Gobind. The return to dust deliberately echoes Salok 178: a brief embodied life can be spent without realizing that purpose. The verse does not make devotion a promise of physical immortality. Its compressed opening still requires grammatical review, with the selected reading kept separate from the source itself.
findings.reason: Explain the corrected grammatical relationship while retaining the mortality context and interpretive status.

findings.before: The first line praises an ordinary meal so warmly that even its salt is nectar. The second asks what price someone would pay for a more desired food. The violent throat image is deliberately severe, especially after Salok 187’s demand for an account of oppression. Together the lines ask the reader to compare nourishment with the moral cost of obtaining pleasure. The Salok’s concrete food words should remain visible; replacing them with a vague lesson about moderation would soften the specific challenge.
findings.after: Khichri and nectar-like salt make modest food attractive before the second line introduces a throat and the wish for meat with bread. The throat’s referent is not explicit. This draft follows the eater’s-own-throat reading displayed under Dr. Sant Singh Khalsa, heard beside 187’s Divine accounting. Sahib Singh instead reads a refusal to slaughter an animal for one’s own meal. Both keep appetite and harm in view; they do not supply the same grammatical subject. The difference needs qualified review and should remain visible.
findings.reason: Replace an unexplained referent choice with a bounded, named comparison while retaining the concrete food and accountability imagery.

findings.before: ਪਹਿਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਸਾਦੇ ਖਾਣੇ ਦੀ ਇੰਨੀ ਕਦਰ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਉਸ ਦਾ ਲੂਣ ਵੀ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਹੈ। ਦੂਜੀ ਪੁੱਛਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਹੋਰ ਚਾਹੇ ਭੋਜਨ ਲਈ ਮਨੁੱਖ ਕਿੰਨੀ ਕੀਮਤ ਦੇਵੇਗਾ। ਗਲਾ ਕਟਣ ਦਾ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਜਾਣ-ਬੁੱਝ ਕੇ ਤਿੱਖਾ ਹੈ, ਖ਼ਾਸ ਕਰਕੇ ੧੮੭ ਦੇ ਜ਼ੁਲਮ ਵਾਲੇ ਲੇਖੇ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ। ਦੋਵੇਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਪੇਟ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਸੁਆਦ ਹਾਸਲ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਨੈਤਿਕ ਕੀਮਤ ਰੱਖਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਭੋਜਨ ਦੇ ਅਸਲ ਨਾਂ ਕਾਇਮ ਰਹਿਣੇ ਚਾਹੀਦੇ ਹਨ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਕੇਵਲ ਸੰਜਮ ਦੀ ਧੁੰਦਲੀ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ ਬਣਾਉਣ ਨਾਲ ਖ਼ਾਸ ਚੁਣੌਤੀ ਹੌਲੀ ਪੈ ਜਾਵੇਗੀ।
findings.after: ਖਿਚੜੀ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵਰਗਾ ਲੂਣ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਸਾਦੇ ਭੋਜਨ ਦੀ ਕਦਰ ਦਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ। ਫਿਰ ਗਲਾ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਸ-ਰੋਟੀ ਦੀ ਚਾਹ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਗਲਾ ਕਿਸ ਦਾ ਹੈ, ਇਹ ਮੂਲ ਤੁਕ ਸਿੱਧਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਦੱਸਦੀ। ਖਰੜਾ ਡਾ. ਸੰਤ ਸਿੰਘ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ ਦੇ ਅਨੁਵਾਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਿੱਸਦੀ ਆਪਣੇ ਗਲੇ ਵਾਲੀ ਪੜ੍ਹਤ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ੧੮੭ ਦੇ ਰੱਬੀ ਲੇਖੇ ਨਾਲ ਪੜ੍ਹਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸਾਹਿਬ ਸਿੰਘ ਆਪਣੇ ਭੋਜਨ ਲਈ ਪਸ਼ੂ ਜ਼ਬਹ ਕਰਨ ਤੋਂ ਇਨਕਾਰ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਦੋਵੇਂ ਚਾਹ ਅਤੇ ਹਾਨੀ ਨੂੰ ਸਾਹਮਣੇ ਰੱਖਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਇੱਕੋ ਵਿਆਕਰਨਕ ਪਾਤਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਦਿੰਦੇ। ਇਹ ਫ਼ਰਕ ਦਿੱਖ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਹੇ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਦਵਾਨੀ ਪਰਖ ਲਈ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਜਾਵੇ।

findings.before: The first line is concrete: bhang, fish and drinking wine are named. The second is equally concrete about the proposed religious counterweight: pilgrimage, fasting and regular observances. The warning says that these practices do not reverse the downward spiritual outcome. Both lists must remain visible for the challenge to retain its force. The verse is not a general statement that any preferred ritual can compensate for any conduct. It specifically refuses that exchange here, placing the direction of lived practice ahead of claims based on religious performance.
findings.after: The first line names bhang, fish and drinking wine. The second names the proposed religious counterweight: pilgrimage, fasting and regular observances. Yet its stated consequence is rasatal, the nether realm of punishment. Both lists and that severe consequence must remain visible. The verse refuses to let these observances cancel the named conduct; it does not merely say that the practices feel disappointing. Its question reaches the direction of lived devotion. The specific warning should remain intact without being expanded into a complete dietary code for every situation.
findings.reason: Preserve the explicit religious consequence alongside the already accurate substances list without manufacturing a comprehensive food rule.

findings.before: ਪਹਿਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਠੋਸ ਹੈ: ਭਾਂਗ, ਮੱਛੀ ਅਤੇ ਸ਼ਰਾਬ ਪੀਣ ਦੇ ਨਾਂ ਹਨ। ਦੂਜੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਤੀਰਥ, ਵਰਤ ਅਤੇ ਨੇਮ ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਹਨ, ਜੋ ਭਰਪਾਈ ਵਜੋਂ ਅੱਗੇ ਰੱਖੇ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਚੇਤਾਵਨੀ ਆਖਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਇਹ ਰਸਮਾਂ ਹੇਠਾਂ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਆਤਮਕ ਫਲ ਨੂੰ ਨਹੀਂ ਮੋੜਦੀਆਂ। ਦੋਵੇਂ ਸੂਚੀਆਂ ਦਿੱਖ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਹਿਣ ਤਾਂ ਹੀ ਪਰਖ ਦੀ ਤਾਕਤ ਕਾਇਮ ਰਹਿੰਦੀ ਹੈ। ਗੱਲ ਇਹ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਿ ਮਨਪਸੰਦ ਰਸਮ ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਕਰਮ ਦੀ ਭਰਪਾਈ ਕਰ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ। ਇੱਥੇ ਉਹ ਸੌਦਾ ਖ਼ਾਸ ਤੌਰ ਉੱਤੇ ਰੱਦ ਹੈ। ਜੀਵੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਦਿਸ਼ਾ ਧਾਰਮਿਕ ਕਾਰਵਾਈ ਦੇ ਦਾਅਵੇ ਤੋਂ ਅੱਗੇ ਰੱਖੀ ਹੈ।
findings.after: ਪਹਿਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਭਾਂਗ, ਮੱਛੀ ਅਤੇ ਸ਼ਰਾਬ ਦੇ ਨਾਂ ਲੈਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਦੂਜੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਤੀਰਥ, ਵਰਤ ਅਤੇ ਨੇਮ ਹਨ, ਜੋ ਭਰਪਾਈ ਵਜੋਂ ਅੱਗੇ ਰੱਖੇ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਫਿਰ ਵੀ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਫਲ ਰਸਾਤਲ, ਨਰਕ ਦਾ ਲੋਕ, ਹੈ। ਦੋਵੇਂ ਸੂਚੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਇਹ ਤਿੱਖਾ ਫਲ ਦਿੱਖ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਹਿਣੇ ਚਾਹੀਦੇ ਹਨ। ਤੁਕ ਇਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਰਸਮਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਨਾਮ ਲਏ ਕਰਮ ਮਿਟਾਉਣ ਨਹੀਂ ਦਿੰਦੀ; ਕੇਵਲ ਨਿਰਾਸ਼ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਨਹੀਂ ਆਖਦੀ। ਪਰਖ ਜੀਵੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਭਗਤੀ ਦੀ ਦਿਸ਼ਾ ਤੱਕ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਖ਼ਾਸ ਚੇਤਾਵਨੀ ਸੰਭਾਲੀ ਰਹੇ, ਪਰ ਇਸ ਤੋਂ ਹਰ ਹਾਲਤ ਲਈ ਭੋਜਨ ਦਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਕਾਨੂੰਨ ਨਾ ਘੜਿਆ ਜਾਵੇ।

retainedAndUnresolvedNotes.note: The bank-full lake reading is supported by the cited lexical explanation of ਪਾਲਿ ਸਮੁਹਾ. It remains a working reading, not a human-approved interpretation.
The ledger distinguishes contextual referents, selected grammatical readings and competing interpretations.
The frozen source U+0A01 in ਗਈਁ remains unchanged. The teaching preserves the distinction between devotional ਭਉ here and fear in 180. No new textual or pagination adjudication is made.
The performer and all-pervading-versus-particular readings match the cited commentary’s selected grammar. The existing competing-reading and qualified-review limits remain.
The vocative duality reading is explicitly attributed. The identity of the six darshans should not be silently expanded into an unreviewed fixed list.
The gain reading of ਲਾਹੂ ਲਾਹਿ matches the selected commentary, and the draft visibly leaves the competing grammar for qualified review.

The draft recognizes observed Mahalla 5 at 209–211, 214 and 221, and Mahalla 3 at 220. It does not automatically transfer these headings to the next unheaded Salok. This is a check against the selected source, not independent human authentication of an edition.

The draft preserves Nama, Trilochan and Ravidas as named textual voices; the Kabir-citing-them interpretation is attributed to Sahib Singh and does not become an automatic canonicalAuthorId assignment.
The dense-forest wording is defensible under Sahib Singh’s Kajali-forest reading. It was not silently replaced with a banana-tree interpretation.
Bhang, fish and wine are all present. Proposed changes clarify rasatal; they do not weaken the named conduct or claim a complete dietary rule.
The head-as-ball image is preserved and immediately identified as devotional self-surrender, not a physical act. No historical episode is fabricated.
The final numbered Salok closes this collection; the draft does not claim to complete Kabir’s Bani elsewhere in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji.
